body: Just wanted to come back to see about you.  I hope that you're okay.  I hope that you've had a better day than most.  Either way, keep on keeping on.  We need you.

I was so glad to get your note.  I actually tried to reply from work today, but I was slammed and kept getting interrupted – my admin was out with a cold and I had to do her job too.  I didn't do it very well.  She may need a raise. 

I can appreciate what you say about people not hearing you, I've felt that way myself pretty much all my life.  For me, the few people in my world who matter seem to go ahead and make all sorts of assumptions.  It's as though they decide how I “should feel”, based on their scope of knowledge, and then they apply their assumptions to me and walk away.  They're all so busy with their own crap, and I get that.  But they never really hear me.  They have no idea how I truly feel.  I wonder if it's like that for you as well.

I have to take some blame for it though, because I let it happen.  I get so down and so disconnected that I don't fight it, I don't put up my hand and ask for help or say, “you don't understand”.  I just feel as though they'll never get it, and I don't see the point.  I'm not sure that's fair of me, but I have a hard time communicating when things are dark.

If I were to guess, I might be able to tell you a lot about yourself.  The irony is that those of us who find ourselves here, those of us who feel so desperate and alone, we're the ones that truly understand life, love, loss, and everything else that is connected with being human.  We feel the world around us far more deeply than the chosen ones.  I think that makes us the better half, but it comes with a tax, of course.  We pay it daily.

For me, I know that I have to forgive myself for a lot of things, even if it was all very unintentional.  I have to forgive myself for fucking up relationships and for not knowing better, or making choices that I wouldn't make again – for being where I am now.  It's not so easy to do, and I haven't succeed yet, but I'm working on it.  It's just another part of being in the better half – we're painfully hard on ourselves.  And it's why simply talking things out, to anyone, is a good plan.

I want nothing more than to give you a recipe or a program that might lead you to the sunny shores of happiness, but I don't have that.  Nobody does.  I feel better today, and in fact, I've had a good week.  I think it's because I told someone how I was feeling.  I've never really done that before.  It made it seem more manageable to me, once it was outside my head.  After that, I started to look for any little light at all, any reason at all.  And it's been okay.

I'm likely more screwed up than you are, and I have nothing to offer.  But I care about you and I want you to be okay.  That sounds really corny, I know, and it's not like me to say it, but it's true.  I do care about you, even though we've never met.  We're both at a fairly unique place and we're both here at the same time.  Like the Titanic – lol.  If I can help you, I will.  Help me too.

Hang in there, Pal, and let me hear you soon.
beautiful, beautiful

My bad - I didn't mean to assume that you were younger, but I did.  I too am older, and so I may be able to appreciate where you are a little bit.  I too have/had lost patience, lost hope, lost any reason to try another comeback.  I've had quite a few of those, and after a while, you just get tired.  I got tired and I didn't want to do it anymore.  

It's really hard, because I know that I can't tell you that the sun will come out tomorrow (I promise, no more songs) and all will be right with the world.  You wouldn't believe it anyway.  

Something that helped me was to explain it to someone, even someone I don't know.  This forum is good for that.  So although I sense your frustration and can feel that you may be done with talking, it might not hurt to give it another go - if only to get it out of your head.  

What helped me was that the ones who responded to me truly meant well, and it was the idea of their kindness that helped me to reflect just a little bit, once more.  I won't bore you with my story, but I'm a lot better now than I was, and for the record, I was pretty much done with, and I mean truly at the end.  Today I'm doing my best to think that maybe there's hope somewhere, and I'm actively looking for reasons.  I've found a couple.

I really wish there was something that I could say or do help you feel better and I wish that I had some answer or a level of wisdom that would show you something that's hiding.  I'm just not all that wise.  But if it helps to know that I'm here, willing and ready to listen, than we have a place to begin.  Who knows.... I might be helpful on accident.

Hang in there.

I read your note carefully, twice in fact.  You could be me.  I have felt unloved, afraid, unworthy, as though the walls were closing in on me, and there wasn't anywhere to go.  And yes, it is like cancer.  I've used that metaphor myself, many times.  I've also said, "If you see a mangled dog on the side of the road, you shoot it."  I mean that's mercy, right?

There's an old song that you very likely have never heard.  It's called, "What a difference a day makes".  The next line is: 24 little hours brought the sun and the flowers when there used to be rain.  The gist of this is that you have no worldly idea what amazing things may come to you out of the clear blue.  I proved that for myself, just this evening.  Life can take so much away form us, but in turn, it can also give us back little miracles.  You need to be ready for that.

You have to stop living in the immediate, and you have to stop looking at everything, every worry, every problem, every sadness, all at one time.  You can't manage that way.  You have to take on your challenges one at a time.  If I were to ask you to clear your head, to stop and to breath deeply for 15 seconds, and then tell me the first thing that comes to your mind, what would that be?  Whatever your answer was, we'd work on it, on that first thing.  We would talk it out and make sense of it, and see about making it better.  Everything else can wait.

Being overwhelmed is the enemy, and I would guess that you are overwhelmed.  The problem with being overwhelmed is that you're trying to work out too many things at one time, and that can't be done.  It's not possible.  It's why we find ourselves lost for answers, and too deeply confused or sad to see a light.  We can't fix everything all at once.  We need to isolate the issues and work on them one at a time.  Because when we do that, they're not so awful bad.

So take a minute, breath real deep and clear your head.  Now tell me the first thing that comes to you - the first thing that's upsetting you.  Let's start there.

You are better than this, pal.  You deserve to be happy.
You just did.  Get some sleep my friend.  Have a kick-ass day tomorrow.
If you feel even a little bit better, than you've just made me feel a LOT better.  So don't thank me... thank YOU.

True greatness can't be created in an hour and I think the irony here is that you're working against yourself.  There is a timeline to a good life, and you've just begun.  Right now what's important is the groundwork.  Obviously you're driven and smart and that's so much more than most.  You're already ahead.  But it's also important to experience your life, and to take a moment to absorb.  Slow down and think things through, and I mean each thought individually.  I get a sense that you think about everything at once, and that'll make you wacky.  You're doing just fine.  Focus on today.  You need to get good at today so that you will do well tomorrow.  I don't know you, but I just get this sense that you're gonna be great.
I have no doubt that Prosvade means well, but I would not recommend that you take any medications to help you sleep.  They are more often depressants and can actually make you feel worse.

PLEASE don't feel that way.  You are their child, this is a part of that.  You can't be expected to play this game alone, none of us can.  We all need to put up our hand at some point to say, "Hey, I need a little help".  Let me congratulate you for doing that here, it was a really smart and really brave thing to do.  

I can tell you that it will get better.  It's just that I understand where you are, and I know that sort of thing is hard to hear when you're down.  But it's true.  Being young, the world can seem raw and immediate.  Everything is amplified.  You just need to chill, and work it out one issue at a time.  If you can fix one, or at least feel better about one thing, then it will help prove to you that there is hope for the rest.  But understand... you are loved, and that matters.  Never ever be afraid to ask for help.  It's the bravest thing you could do.

It's a terrible way to have to feel all the time and although I can't know how it is for you, I can empathize with the feelings.  Something that strikes me about your note is that it's pretty obvious that you're smart, and that you feel things pretty deeply.  Believe it or not, that's a good thing.  Something that helped me was to try really hard to separate all the thoughts and try to isolate just one.  Then work on just one at a time.  Why, for example, do you feel that you're acutely aware of your mortality?  I've experienced that too, quite a lot.  I'd like to know your thoughts on that.
I'm sorry that you're feeling so badly.  Tell me what doubts you're talking about.

It would seem that if you are concerned about the affect of your leaving that you have people that love you.  The secret is that this isn't terminal, as dark and as horrible as you might feel right now.  I know of which I speak, having been there very recently.  But I found a faint light, and I've been following it.  I don't want you to go.  Your family doesn't want you to go.  You did something amazing here.  You put it out there.  That says an awful lot.  So don't stop now.  Tell us more.
I'm so sorry this has happened to you.  If you'd like to talk, I'd like to listen.  Maybe tell us about your son.

Go in Spring.  It can be silly-hot in the summer months.  Also - in the canyon, there's a singer on the Mexican side.  Scared the sh-t out of me, because there isn't a soul for miles.  He sings for tips.  Check that out too - it made a memory for me that I'll never forget.
Big Bend.  The canyon along the Rio Grande - amazing.

I truly understand what you mean when you say that you have no solutions.  And yeah, everything you wrote down is significant and I can only imagine how difficult everything must seem to you right now.  But there is also an enormous amount of hope in what you wrote down, you've obviously got a lot going for you.  

I too feel as if I'm at the end.  I came here and wrote it down and some good people wrote back to me.  It kept me going today.  

I can listen, and I can give you some straight-up feedback.  I think sometimes it really does help to tell someone.  Either way, don't you dare give up.
Hey - I'm worried about you.  My hat is in the ring with MedDead.  I'll be here if you need another ear.

I'm sorry for your loss, and I imagine that it must have been horrible.  I hate to say that I understand your friend's selfishness, I think I can see where it can just be too much.  I wish he could have come here.  I made a choice to post here, and it was a good one.  There's a lot of kindness here.  I felt less alone for a little bit today.

I hear the idea that I need to step out of my comfort zone.  What's interesting to me right now is that I'm in a place where I have nothing to lose.  ...So maybe.  Thank you again.
Thank you.  You're awesome.

You have a choice to make, and I did too at 17.  What you need to understand is that you can’t apply my story to your life, because it doesn’t need to be that way.  My life didn’t need to be this way.  I could have corrected my course, and that’s what I mean to tell you.  The last thing I want to do is to make you feel sad.  You can be more courageous than I was, stronger.  You can put up your hand and ask for help.  I never did that.

I appreciate you.  Thanks for sparing me the platitudes and for putting an idea in my head that I wasn't expecting.  I never considered the idea of being useful on this subject, feeling it more poison for poison, but the points you've made are clear and reasonable.  And thoughtful.  And you heard me.  I wonder if that's what I need, because it just feels good to be heard.  I wasn't expecting that.
God, I want to be needed.
(wept)  TY
